title: Auditing our own live P&L
hypothesis: The live paper-trading P&L measures the strategies, not the plumbing.
question: Were the live numbers on the dashboard real?
prior: A live track is only evidence if its accounting is right.
method: Checked every live track against accounting invariants: cash + net = equity, gross ≥ |net|, P&L = change in equity.
Replayed the fill-based tracks from inception under the fixed accounting.
verdict_reason: They were not. A data merge replaced 500 days of history with one row, missing prices fell back to cost, exposure was marked at cost, and there was no buying-power check. Markowitz reached 240% gross with negative cash. All fixed and replayed; the deep-RL vol agent was retired (it had converged to equal weight).
lessons: Check a live-vs-backtest gap against the same calendar window in the backtest before calling it a defect.
Trace a one-day spike to its ticker before calling it a bug (the +7.8% Markowitz day was a real MRNA move).
footer: Research code is private; methods summarised below.
